change_summary: The editors first issued an expression of concern about the calculation of the dose-response analysis. They then retracted the article and replaced it with a corrected version. The Table 3 slope was miscalculated: reported as 0.45 points per 10 mg, correct value 0.28. The stored paper reports a slope of 0.45 points per 10 mg (95% CI 0.30 to 0.60), while the corrected version reports 0.28 points per 10 mg (95% CI 0.15 to 0.41). The notice says the finding that iron supplementation reduces fatigue is unchanged.
evaluation: Your Discussion cites Park and Singh [7] and compares your slope of 0.41 with their 0.45 per 10 mg. The stored paper reports that 0.45 slope, but the retraction notice says the slope was reported as 0.45 points per 10 mg and the correct value is 0.28 points per 10 mg. The corrected version reports 0.28 points per 10 mg (95% CI 0.15 to 0.41), so the comparison figure in your Discussion is the one that changed. The notice says the finding that iron supplementation reduces fatigue is unchanged. Because this is only a comparison with your own result, the overall impact on your draft is low.
recommendation: Your Discussion compares your slope of 0.41 per 10 mg with Park and Singh's 0.45 per 10 mg and says this supports the validity of your design, but the retraction notice says the slope was reported as 0.45 points per 10 mg and the correct value is 0.28 points per 10 mg. Replace 0.45 with 0.28 in that sentence and re-check whether your slope still supports the validity of your design. The article was retracted and replaced by a corrected version, so cite the replacement. The notice says the finding that iron supplementation reduces fatigue is unchanged, but confirm that in the corrected version before updating the reference.
